incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, as amended; in particular sections governing incorporation (s. 10), articles (ss. 6-9), registered office and records (ss. 24-25), directors and officers (ss. 99-106), share allotment (ss. 25-29) and provisions applicable to unlimited liability corporations (s. 15 and related regulations).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta, Government of Alberta (online filing via authorized Alberta Registry Agents).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Unlimited Liability Company) issued with a Certificate of Incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement under Alberta law. Shares may be issued for nominal or deferred consideration, but any uncalled or unpaid share capital of a ULC may be subject to collection by the directors or creditors on winding up and the shareholders' liability is unlimited.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the subscription by each named subscriber, as set out in the Share Allocation Schedule, to such number of Common and Special shares as listed with consideration credited to issued share capital is approved and ratified. That the registered office of the Company be fixed at Suite 1000, 333 Seventh Avenue SW, Calgary, Alberta, T2P 2Z1, Canada, and the Registered Office Adoption Agreement be executed by the Chair. That the following persons are appointed as officers: Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, Secretary, and Treasurer, each with authority to execute banking and wire transfer mandates, vendor agreements, and regulatory filings. All prior acts in connection with incorporation are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry – Name Approval Unit, accessed through a licensed Alberta Registry Agent or the Corporate Registry's online search portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS name search request through an authorized Alberta Registry Agent, providing the proposed corporate name followed by 'Unlimited Liability Company' or 'ULC'. Verify that the name is distinctive and not confusingly similar to existing Alberta or extra-provincial names. Reserve the approved name for up to 90 days if a priority reservation is required. Retain the search report for attachment to the Articles of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and corporate suffix
NUANS name search request form
Description of proposed business activities (if requested)
Authorized registry agent retainer or online filing consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or queried on distinctiveness grounds, file a revised name or obtain written consent from the holder of the conflicting name. If the Registrar issues a formal name refusal, submit a reconsideration request with supporting arguments and comparable name evidence in accordance with the Alberta name approval policy.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Electronic Filing of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) via an authorized Registry Agent or the provincial online incorporation system.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the prescribed Articles of Incorporation form, expressly electing the unlimited liability corporation type. Include the reserved name, the street address of the registered office (a physical Alberta address, not a post office box), the share capital structure including classes and any par value or special rights, and the names plus residential addresses of all initial directors. Attach the NUANS report and the signed consent of each director. File electronically and pay the applicable registry fee. The Registrar will then issue the Certificate of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: NUANS name search report
Articles of Incorporation (Alberta ULC election)
Consent to Act as Director for each initial director
Registered office street address in Alberta
Government-issued identification and residential addresses of directors and incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a deficiency notice, correct the described omissions and resubmit the amended articles. If the Certificate of Incorporation is issued with a clerical error, submit a formal correction request to the Registrar within the statutory correction period or apply for a rectification order from the court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office Adoption, Corporate Records Address, and Statutory Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry; corporate services provider maintaining the registered office and corporate records address.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, execute the Registered Office Adoption Agreement with the corporate services provider or landlord confirming the physical address stated in the Articles. Establish the records address where the corporate records, share register, and minutes book will be maintained. Verify that the registered office location and records address conform to the Business Corporations Act (Alberta). File any subsequent 'Notice of Change of Registered Office' or 'Notice of Change of Directors' with the Corporate Registry, if applicable.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Articles of Incorporation
Registered Office Adoption Agreement
Corporate lease or occupation consent
Initial share register and corporate minute book
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the chosen office provider rejects the adoption agreement, select an alternative Alberta physical address, execute a new adoption agreement, and submit a change of registered office notice to the Corporate Registry before the required filing deadline. Any Registry objection can be cured by filing the corrected notice and supporting documentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Resolution: Share Subscription, Officer Appointments, and Banking Mandates
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Board of Directors (internal corporate governance; no separate government filing).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first organizational meeting of the board of directors, either physically or by written unanimous resolution. Approve the subscription and allotment of shares as set out in the Share Allocation Schedule, ratify the registered office adoption, appoint the Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, Secretary, and Treasurer, adopt the corporate by-laws including banking and wire transfer authorization provisions, and authorize officers to execute agreements and filings. Record all resolutions in signed minutes in the corporate minute book.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and Articles of Incorporation
Initial directors' consents to act
Share subscription and allocation schedule
Officer appointment consents
Draft board resolution and banking mandate forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director or officer objects to any appointment or allotment, ratify the decision through a further unanimous consent resolution or by a vote at a duly convened board meeting. Ensure that all consents and resolutions are formally recorded to cure any governance defect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Canada Revenue Agency Tax Registrations and Alberta Provincial Tax Coordination
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – Business Registration Online; Alberta Finance and the CRA for combined federal and provincial corporate income tax.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the new corporation with the CRA to obtain a nine-digit Business Number (BN). Open the corporation income tax account (RT) and, if taxable sales exceed CAD 30,000 in any quarter or if the company voluntarily elects, register for the GST/HST account (RT). If employees will be hired, register for the payroll deductions account (RP) and comply with workers' compensation board registration in Alberta. Alberta corporate income tax is reported through the single CRA T2 corporate return; no separate provincial incorporation filing fee is required.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and Articles of Incorporation
Corporate registered office and records address
Directors' and officers' residential addresses and social insurance numbers
Corporate authorization form (for representatives)
Projected gross revenue and expected GST/HST registration threshold analysis
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA issues a compliance or verification letter, provide the requested supporting records through Business Registration Online or by correspondence. Any error in the Business Number or program accounts can be corrected by filing an amendment via a CRA authorized representative. Maintain all CRA confirmation numbers in the corporate records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence and Occupational and Fire Safety Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: City of Calgary or City of Edmonton Business Licensing and Safety Codes Services; Alberta Fire Code enforcement authorities.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a municipal general business licence where the local by-law requires one for the office-based newswire and financial news aggregation operation. Obtain the occupancy permit or certificate for the leased premises and arrange a safety codes review confirming compliance with structural load, electrical, and fire safety requirements under the Alberta Fire Code. Provide the municipal licensing office with the Certificate of Incorporation, lease agreement, and proof of insurance. Register with the provincial Workers' Compensation Board if payroll thresholds are met or if any employees are engaged.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and Articles of Incorporation
Office lease agreement and floor plan
Municipal business licence application form
Occupancy permit / safety codes inspection report
Commercial general liability insurance certificate
Fire safety plan and fire extinguisher inspection record
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If municipal licensing or fire safety inspectors identify deficiencies, submit revised floor plans, install required equipment, and obtain re-inspection certificates. The company may appeal an adverse municipal licensing decision through the local property standards and licence appeal committee within the prescribed appeal period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipal Business Licensing and Safety Codes Services (City of Calgary or City of Edmonton); no sectoral industrial licensing board applies to ISIC 6391 financial news aggregation and syndication services.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: General Business Licence and Building Occupancy Permit (office use only; no statutory manufacturing or financial services licence required)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – office-based information services; no Environmental Impact Assessment or registration is required under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act, and no listed activity under the Activities Designation Regulation is triggered.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharge or VOC emissions are generated. Comply with municipal solid waste and electronic waste diversion requirements under applicable Alberta recycling and waste management codes. Office refrigeration and HVAC equipment must contain approved refrigerants and be serviced in accordance with the Alberta Ozone-Depleting Substances and Halocarbons Regulation, and all data center electronics must be disposed through licensed electronic recyclers.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The premises must obtain a fire safety codes clearance in accordance with the Alberta Fire Code, including acceptable structural load ratings, adequate means of egress, and fire extinguisher inspection. An Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) workplace clearance under the Occupational Health and Safety Act, RSA 2000, c O-2, and the Alberta OHS Code is required for the newswire operations, covering emergency response planning, ergonomics for prolonged computer use, and any network equipment electrical safety certificates.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), operating through Business Registration Online (BRO) and My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-login-services.html); Alberta corporate income tax and federal GST are assessed and collected by CRA on behalf of the Province of Alberta under the Canada-Alberta Tax Collection Agreement; no separate Alberta tax agency is involved for GST or corporate income tax administration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Alberta ULC must first obtain a Business Number (BN) by submitting CRA Form RC1 or, where a Canadian representative is authorized, through Business Registration Online. CRA issues a 9-digit BN with program account suffixes: RC (corporate income tax), RT (GST/HST), RU (import/export account) as applicable. Standard processing for paper Form RC1 is five to ten business days; online issuance is immediate when identity and corporate existence are verified. The foreign parent must provide Alberta certificate of incorporation, registered office address, director/shareholder details, and foreign registration documents. No physical Canadian presence is required, but a resident agent or authorized representative is advisable for service of notices.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — for Canadian income tax purposes the ULC is mandatorily a resident corporation taxed at entity level (federal 15% plus Alberta 8%, combined headline rate 23%); the unlimited liability feature allows shareholders in certain foreign jurisdictions, notably the United States, to check the box and treat the ULC as a disregarded entity or partnership for foreign tax purposes only. CRA does not recognize the ULC as fiscally transparent for Canadian tax purposes, creating hybrid entity and reverse hybrid mismatch risk requiring BEPS Action 2 analysis. For GST/HST purposes the ULC is a distinct registrant.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no domestic check-the-box election. Available statutory mechanisms relevant to an AB ULC engaged in financial newswire services include: (i) ETA s. 241 simplified GST/HST registration election for non-residents who do not carry on business in Canada, used to recover GST on Canadian establishment costs; (ii) ETA s. 156(2) election for closely related corporations to deem supplies for nil consideration; (iii) ITA s. 249.1 election to adopt a non-calendar taxation year; (iv) foreign shareholders separately file US Form 8832 with the IRS, an election not binding on CRA. Canadian hybrid mismatch rules (ITA ss. 18.2, 18.3 and the reverse-hybrid rules in s. 20.2) apply to payments after the relevant effective dates and may deny deductions or impose withholding adjustments where a ULC is treated as transpterent offshore.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-added tax branded as GST/HST under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act (Canada); Alberta has no provincial retail sales tax, so the sole indirect tax in CA-AB is the federal 5% GST, with no HST provincial component.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in worldwide taxable supplies, other than zero-rated and exempt supplies, computed over any four consecutive calendar quarters under the small supplier rules (ETA s. 148). A non-resident carrying on business in Canada that meets or exceeds this threshold is required to register for GST/HST; a non-resident not carrying on business in Canada may nevertheless voluntarily register under the simplified regime. For a syndicated finance newswire API, CRA will assess Canadian nexus based on place of negotiation, Canadian subscribers or users, server location, and whether services are performed in Canada.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory continuous transaction controls, real-time fiscal clearance, or digital stamping exists in Canada. CRA accepts EDI, XML, PDF, and PEPPOL-bis electronic invoices; registrants with annual taxable supplies above CAD 1,000,000 must file GST/HST returns electronically through GST/HST NETFILE or TEI. Records must be retained in readable electronic format for six years under ETA s. 286 and CRA Information Circular IC05-1. Voluntary e-invoicing is being standardized via the Pan-Canadian Trust Framework and PEPPOL for federal procurement, but no tax-clearance API applies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The syndicated financial newswire and API data feed qualifies as a supply of a service and is zero-rated under ETA Schedule VI, Part V, s. 7 where the recipient is a non-resident person who is not registered for GST/HST and the service is not performed in connection with real property or tangible personal property situated in Canada. The service is not a financial service under ETA Schedule V, Part VII, and therefore does not fall into the exempt category; aggregation of market news, API access rights, and syndicated data distribution are ancillary information services, enabling the exporter to claim 0%. Canadian-resident subscribers attract 5% GST in Alberta.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CBSA Form B13A or EDI/eManifest record) for any tangible media shipped outside Canada; for pure API services, the signed subscription order and delivery log serve as the export-control evidence.
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill for physical exports and, for digital delivery, a server access log and API usage report demonstrating transmission to the non-resident recipient.
Inward Remittance Certificate, SWIFT MT103, or exporting gateway reconciliation showing settlement from a non-resident account into the Alberta ULC bank account.
Valid export contract or master services agreement identifying the non-resident customer, governing law, place of consumption, and zero-rating provision.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess zero-rated export supplies within the normal four-year assessment period (ETA ss. 296-298) where export documentation is incomplete; the limitation period is indefinite where misrepresentation, neglect, or wilful default is established. This structure treats the 180-day FX repatriation figure as an internal export-control benchmark, because the ETA imposes no express statutory repatriation deadline; exporters are advised to document remittance within 180 days to support the non-resident nature of the receivable. Civil penalties include ETA s. 280 failure-to-file or failure-to-register penalties of CAD 250 plus CAD 25 per day (maximum CAD 2,500), and s. 285 false-statement penalties of up to CAD 25,000. Fraudulent export zero-rating is an indictable offence under ETA s. 327 carrying fines of up to double the tax avoided and imprisonment up to two years. CRA may also recover undeposited GST, charge prescribed daily interest, and apply GAAR or hybrid-mismatch provisions if the zero-rating is used to engineer an artificial loss or reverse-hybrid deduction.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) as central monetary institution; prudential supervision of deposit-taking institutions exercised by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); cross-border currency and wire-transaction reporting administered by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA); overall foreign-exchange policy authority resides with the Department of Finance Canada. Canada has no dedicated foreign-exchange-control licensing body and no exchange-control statute.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada adheres to IMF Article VIII: both current-account and capital-account transactions are fully convertible, with no exchange-control approvals, no local-reinvestment condition, and no restriction on dividend, interest, royalty, or service-fee remittance by non-resident shareholders or group companies. The only fiscal frictions on profit repatriation from an Alberta ULC to a US parent are Part XIII withholding taxes (statutory 25% on dividends and certain outbound payments, generally reduced to 5% on dividends under the Canada-US Tax Convention of 1980) and the documentary burden of treaty-benefit certification. The Article XIII unlimited-liability-company relief, combined with a valid US check-the-box election under Treasury Regulation §301.7701-3, allows a wholly-owned US corporation to obtain cash flows from the Alberta ULC without Canadian withholding leakage on a deemed dividend, provided the US parent files an NR301 treaty-entitlement certificate or IRS Form 6166 with the paying bank. No economic-substance requirement, capital-control permit, or balance-of-payments authorization applies to profit remittance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None: Canadian federal and Alberta statutes impose no export-proceeds surrender obligation, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no repatriation timeline for foreign-currency receipts. The sole legal duties are (i) the reporting of every cross-border wire transfer of CAD 10,000 or more by the financial institution to FINTRAC as an electronic funds transfer report (EFTR); (ii) declaration to the Canada Border Services Agency of any physical currency or monetary instrument of CAD 10,000 or more under the Cross-Border Currency and Monetary Instruments Reporting Regulations (PCMLTFA); and (iii) retention of books and records for at least five years under the PCMLTFA and the Income Tax Act, including recognition of foreign-exchange gains and losses on disposition of export or subscription proceeds.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Conditional Medium: Canada-regulated payment service providers and global fintech processors are viable collection-layer utilities, but offshore electronic-money institutions are not acceptable as primary treasury custodians. Stripe Payments Canada, Ltd. and Wise Canada, Ltd., as entities registered or in the process of registration under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA, administered by the Bank of Canada), may open merchant or payout accounts for a Canadian-domiciled ULC and clear CAD-denominated subscription receipts from API feed clients; however, they do not hold a Bank Act banking licence, cannot clear directly over Lynx or Canadian EFT rails, and cannot custody multi-million-dollar capital injections. Offshore digital EMIs domiciled in the UK, EU, or EEA are of marginal utility: they generally decline unlimited-liability corporate structures in their risk scoring, cannot register with FINTRAC as reporting entities for Canadian-origin flows, cannot open CAD domestic settlement accounts, and lack direct access to Canadian clearing infrastructure. Feasibility rating: High for Stripe or Wise as merchant-acquiring and low-value disbursement rails; Low for any offshore EMI as a treasury or escrow depositary. Recommended architecture: maintain one Schedule I bank operating account and a segregated capital-escrow account, with Stripe used solely as a low-value subscription collection switch feeding the bank account daily.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: De facto physical-presence mandate applies. Under the client-identification and record-keeping obligations of the PCMLTFA and prevailing Schedule I bank policies, at least one director, one 25-percent-plus beneficial owner, or one senior authorized signing officer must appear in person at a Canadian branch or before a Canadian notary public or lawyer retained by the bank as a verification agent; non-resident directors may be identified remotely only through originals or certified copies with notarial seals and, where required, apostille or consular legalization. Pure video-only remote onboarding is generally not offered for a 100-percent-foreign-owned Alberta ULC operating as a digital newswire API. Practical expediting rule: appoint a Canadian resident director or a Canadian-resident corporate counsel as a signing officer; expect to deliver an original board resolution authenticated by the corporate secretary, certified identification for each director, and personal attendance of at least one signatory at account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unlimited-liability corporate name and structure: automated open-account engines and credit scoring treat 'ULC' as an anomalous or high-risk entity form due to shareholder exposure to third-party claims, prompting enhanced due diligence or outright decline.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (i) certified Alberta Articles of Incorporation or continued articles under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9 showing unlimited-liability status; (ii) Alberta Corporate Registry current search report; (iii) a Canadian legal opinion explaining that the unlimited-liability feature is a statutory pass-through mechanism for US tax efficiency and does not alter the low-risk factual profile of a financial-market-data API business; (iv) an executed unlimited-liability acknowledgment letter addressed to the bank confirming that shareholders and directors understand the residual liability; (v) a bank-grade adverse-media report in the entity's name.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: 100-percent non-resident US ownership with no Canadian director or visible Canadian wealth and a large capital injection; possible suspicion of unexplained wealth or conduits for tax evasion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (i) two years of audited or compiled financial statements of the US parent; (ii) funding-bank reference letters with 24-month account statements; (iii) corporate resolutions authorizing the equity injection and share issuance; (iv) a source-of-funds declaration tracing the injection to the parent's disclosed operating income or committed credit facilities; (v) the IRS Form 8832 check-the-box election establishing the ULC's disregarded-entity purpose; (vi) completed FATCA Form W-8BEN-E, CRS self-certification, and NR301 treaty-benefit form; (vii) an intercompany services or license agreement supporting future cash-flow logic.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Digital and API-only business model with no physical Canadian sales office, minimal fixed assets, and concentration of revenue in B2B syndication licenses; misclassification of ISIC 6391 news aggregation as media or politically exposed activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (i) ISIC 6391 / NAICS 519110 industry-code certification from the entity's registration records; (ii) executed subscriber and API-license agreements demonstrating financial-market news aggregation, not general news or public-relations activity; (iii) technical documentation of the financial newswire feed and platform redundancy; (iv) invoice samples and the expected transaction-flow map; (v) an internal AML risk memorandum aligning the business to the bank's Low_Risk_Standard tier; (vi) trademark registrations and the active operational website for the feed product.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity: absence of a disclosed individuals-with-significant-control register, use of corporate trustees, or nominee-looking directors may trigger FINTRAC and bank political-exposure-person review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (i) the ULC's register of individuals with significant control (ISC) prepared in compliance with the Alberta Business Corporations Act; (ii) a signed beneficial-ownership matrix identifying every direct and indirect 25-percent-or-greater owner; (iii) an affirmative declaration that no nominee shareholdings, bearer instruments, or undisclosed trusts exist; (iv) the current Alberta Corporate Registry filing excerpt for the ULC; (v) if a professional service firm provides registered-office or corporate-secretary services, the executed engagement letter naming the firm and its regulatory registrations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Service Alberta Corporate Registry (Registrar of Corporations)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two months after the anniversary date of incorporation each year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment attracts a registry late-service fee; failure to file for two consecutive years may trigger administrative dissolution. Reinstatement requires settlement of all arrears plus a revival fee.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after taxation year-end; tax balance due two months after year-end (three months for an eligible Canadian-controlled private corporation).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty under Income Tax Act s. 162(2): 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month up to 12 months; no administrative strike-off, but criminal sanctions may apply for repeated non-filing.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Alberta Business Corporations Act, a private corporation may waive the appointment of an auditor by unanimous shareholders' consent; absent waiver, an independent audit and audited financial statements are required regardless of revenue or asset size.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or ASPE (Canadian accounting standards for private enterprises); IFRS is required for publicly accountable entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta does not require a separate annual UBO declaration, but the Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) must be continuously updated within 15 days of any change and be produced to the Registrar on demand; the annual return attests that the registered office and director information is accurate.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays; general deductions and credits apply (e.g., SR&ED, investment tax credits). Alberta does not offer provincial tax holidays.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return; filed electronically via CRA NETFILE or through a tax preparer using CRA-approved software.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Six months after the fiscal year-end (e.g., if FYE Dec 31, due June 30).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business income (or loss) from operations, including revenue from syndicated financial news feeds.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Not applicable to non-resident shareholders; this field is for the resident corporation's income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after deductions, including capital cost allowance, reserves, and loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Not applicable to non-resident shareholders; this field is for the resident corporation's taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal and provincial tax payable before credits, calculated at the combined 23% rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Not applicable to non-resident shareholders; this field is for the resident corporation's tax liability.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total tax credits (e.g., foreign tax credits, investment tax credits) and provincial credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Not applicable to non-resident shareholders; this field is for the resident corporation's credits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax payable or refund due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Not applicable to non-resident shareholders; this field is for the resident corporation's final tax position.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month up to 12 months (max 17%). Repeated failure: additional 10% penalty. Interest on late payments at prescribed rates (currently ~9% annually).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders under Canadian domestic law.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced treaty rate (e.g., 15% under Canada-US treaty, or 5% for corporate shareholders owning ≥10% voting shares), the non-resident shareholder must provide a Certificate of Residency (Form NR301) and complete Form NR302 (Waiver) or NR303 (Reduced Rate) to the paying corporation. The payer must retain these documents and remit the reduced WHT to CRA.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: interest 25% (exempt for arm's length), royalties 25%. Treaty rates (Canada-US): interest 0% for arm's length, royalties 10% for certain IP (e.g., copyright, patent). Other treaties may vary.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Contemporaneous documentation required if total value of transactions with each non-resident non-arm's length party exceeds CAD 1 million for goods, CAD 500,000 for services, or CAD 250,000 for intangibles.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: No specific Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) in Canada; however, the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) and substance-over-form principles apply. Transactions must have genuine economic substance to avoid recharacterization.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully omitting income, falsifying records, or making false statements to CRA to reduce tax liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under Income Tax Act s.239: fine up to 200% of tax evaded and/or imprisonment up to 5 years. Civil penalties: 50% gross negligence penalty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for unpaid corporate taxes under s.227.1 if they failed to withhold/remit. Civil restitution, travel bans, and imprisonment possible.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a conduit with no real business activity, employees, or assets, solely to avoid tax or launder funds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR reassessment, denial of treaty benefits, and penalties up to 25% of tax avoided. CRA may also impose third-party penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held liable for unpaid taxes if they knowingly participated in a sham arrangement. Personal assets may be seized.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to register as a money services business (MSB) if providing financial services, or failure to report suspicious transactions to FINTRAC.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalties up to CAD 2 million for corporations, criminal fines up to CAD 500,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years for individuals.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally fined or imprisoned if they knowingly fail to comply with AML obligations. Travel bans may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to maintain contemporaneous documentation or applying non-arm's length pricing resulting in understated income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income, penalties up to 10% of net adjustment (if gross negligence), and interest on underpaid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for penalties if they signed false or misleading returns. Civil restitution and potential criminal charges for willful evasion.
